brief.subject: IRS finalizes rules for paying taxes directly by card
brief.headline: IRS Final Rules Clear the Way to Take Card Payments Directly
brief.dek: New IRS regs on card payments, a preparer charged over 4,335 returns, Colorado's tax ballot fight and two corporate tax updates.
brief.lede: The IRS has finalized regulations letting it accept credit and debit card tax payments directly, without routing taxpayers through outside processors.

sections.heading: IRS Can Now Take Cards Directly
bullets: Final regulations published 2026-10-19 implement Taxpayer First Act changes on paying tax by commercially acceptable means.
The IRS may accept credit or debit card payments itself, rather than connecting payers to third-party processors.
The rules also lift limits on the IRS paying fees under contracts tied to card-based tax payments.
For owners who pay estimates by card, watch for changes in how card payments are handled.

sections.heading: Preparer Charged Over 4,335 Returns
bullets: Yuridia Trujillo, 43, of Meriden, CT, was arrested and accused of filing 4,335 fraudulent returns through her tax business.
The charges are allegations; the case is a reminder to vet any preparer handling your business or personal filings.

sections.heading: Colorado Tax Measure Stays on Ballot
bullets: A Denver District Court judge ruled Wednesday that a graduated income tax proposal can remain on Colorado's November ballot.
The measure would replace the state's flat income tax rate, affecting pass-through owners who pay tax at individual rates.
The legal challenge to the measure is not over.

sections.heading: Corporate and Court Tax Watch
bullets: The IRS partially withdrew proposed Section 355 rules on the device test and active trade or business requirement.
Those rules govern tax-free distributions of controlled corporation stock, so corporations planning spinoffs should check with advisors.
The Tax Court disallowed deductions for historic structure conservation easements, another setback for easement write-offs.

items.title: Proposed Rule: Guidance Under Section 355 Concerning Device and Active Trade or Business; Partial Withdrawal
items.snippet: This document partially withdraws a notice of proposed rulemaking containing proposed regulations regarding the application of the device prohibition and the active trade or business requirement for distributions of controlled corporation stock (or stock and securities) by a distributing corporation without income, gain, or loss. The proposed regulations would affect corporations and their shareholders and security holders.

items.title: Rule: Regulations Regarding Payment of Tax by Commercially Acceptable Means
items.snippet: This document contains final regulations regarding the payment of tax by commercially acceptable means. The final regulations reflect changes to the law made by the Taxpayer First Act that would allow the IRS to directly accept payments of tax by credit or debit card, without having to connect taxpayers to third-party payment processors. These final regulations remove restrictions on the payment of any fee by the IRS under any contracts related to payment of taxes by credit, debit, or charge car
